arXiv:math/0604134v2 [math.AG] 13 Jun 2007

Formal structure of direct image of holonomic 𝒟\mathcal{D}-modules of exponential type

Céline Roucairol Address: Lehrstuhl VI für Math., Univ. Mannheim, A5 6, 68161 Mannheim, Germany. Email address: celine.roucairol@uni-mannheim.de
Abstract.

We compute formal invariants associated with the cohomology sheaves of the direct image of holonomic 𝒟\mathcal{D}-modules of exponential type. We also prove that every formal ℂ[[t]]⟨∂t⟩\mathbb{C}[[t]]\langle\partial_{t}\rangle-modules is isomorphic, after a ramification, to a germ of formalized direct image of analytic 𝒟\mathcal{D}-module of exponential type.

1991 Mathematics Subject Classification
32S40, 32C38, 34M35

Introduction

Let XX be a complex manifold. We denote by 𝒪X\mathcal{O}_{X} (resp. 𝒟X\mathcal{D}_{X}) the sheaf of holomorphic functions (resp. holomorphic differential operators) on XX. For any reduced divisor ZZ in XX, we denote by 𝒪X[∗Z]\mathcal{O}_{X}[\ast Z] the sheaf of meromorphic functions with poles along ZZ at most. Given a regular holonomic 𝒟X\mathcal{D}_{X}-module ℳ\mathcal{M} and a meromorphic function gg on XX with poles along ZZ, we define the 𝒟X\mathcal{D}_{X}-module ℳ​eg\mathcal{M}e^{g} as being the 𝒪X\mathcal{O}_{X}-module ℳ[∗Z]:=𝒪X[∗Z]⊗𝒪Xℳ\mathcal{M}[\ast Z]:=\mathcal{O}_{X}[\ast Z]\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}\mathcal{M} with connection ∇g\nabla_{g} defined as ∇+d​g\nabla+dg, where ∇\nabla is the connection on ℳ[∗Z]\mathcal{M}[\ast Z] given by its left 𝒟X\mathcal{D}_{X}-module structure. It is known that ℳ​eg\mathcal{M}e^{g} is a holonomic 𝒟X\mathcal{D}_{X}-module. It is irregular along ZZ. We will say ℳ​eg\mathcal{M}e^{g} has exponential type.

In the algebraic setting, if UU is a smooth algebraic variety over ℂ\mathbb{C}, we use an exponent “alg\mathrm{alg}” in the notation of the corresponding sheaves and we define the notion of a holonomic 𝒟Xalg\mathcal{D}_{X}^{\mathrm{alg}}-module of exponential type similarly.

Let ℳ​eg\mathcal{M}e^{g} be a holonomic 𝒟X\mathcal{D}_{X}-module of exponential type. The cohomology sheaves of its direct image by any proper map f:X→Cf:X\to C to a complex curve are holonomic 𝒟C\mathcal{D}_{C}-modules with possibly irregular singularities. The main result of this article consists in the computation of the formal invariants of these cohomology modules at their singularities.

The basic computation takes place in the following setting: the complex manifold XX is the product D×ℙ1D\times\mathbb{P}^{1} of a small disc DD centered at the origin in ℂ\mathbb{C} by the Riemann sphere, the meromorphic function gg is the projection p2:X→ℙ1p_{2}:X\to\mathbb{P}^{1} with polar divisor Z=D×{∞}Z=D\times\{\infty\} and the map ff is the projection p1:X→Dp_{1}:X\to D. We will denote by tt a coordinate on DD. As above, ℳ\mathcal{M} is a regular holonomic 𝒟X\mathcal{D}_{X}-module. The only interesting cohomology module to consider is 𝒩=ℋ0​p1+​(ℳ​ep2)\mathcal{N}=\mathcal{H}^{0}p_{1+}(\mathcal{M}e^{p_{2}}) and we assume that DD is small enough so that 00 is the only singular point of 𝒩\mathcal{N}.

In a neighbourhood UU of (0,∞)∈D×ℙ1(0,\infty)\in D\times\mathbb{P}^{1}, the singular support of ℳ\mathcal{M} is an analytic curve SS. We denote by {Sℓ∣ℓ∈Λ}\{S_{\ell}\mid\ell\in\Lambda\} the set consisting of the local irreducible components of SS which are distinct of {0}×ℙ1\{0\}\times\mathbb{P}^{1} or D×{∞}D\times\{\infty\}. We shall assume that the reader is familiar with the definitions and the properties of the specialization functor and the nearby cycles functor for 𝒟\mathcal{D}-modules along a hypersurface and we refer to [4], [9], [17], [7] and [8] for details. Given Y⊂XY\subset X a smooth hypersurface of XX defined by a global equation h=0h=0 and given ℳ\mathcal{M} a specializable 𝒟X\mathcal{D}_{X}-module, we will denote by spY⁡ℳ\spe_{Y}\mathcal{M} the specialization of ℳ\mathcal{M} along YY and by Ψh​ℳ\Psi_{h}\mathcal{M} the nearby cycle module of ℳ\mathcal{M} along YY. If V∙​ℳV_{\bullet}\mathcal{M} is the canonical V-filtration with respect to the lexical order on ℂ≃ℝ⊕i​ℝ\mathbb{C}\simeq\mathbb{R}\oplus i\mathbb{R}, spYℳ=⊕β∈ℂVβℳ/V<βℳ\spe_{Y}\mathcal{M}=\oplus_{\beta\in\mathbb{C}}{V_{\beta}\mathcal{M}}/{V_{<\beta}\mathcal{M}} and Ψhℳ=⊕−1≤β<0Vβℳ/V<βℳ\Psi_{h}\mathcal{M}=\oplus_{-1\leq\beta<0}{V_{\beta}\mathcal{M}}/{V_{<\beta}\mathcal{M}}. Same definitions hold for YY hypersurface with normal crossings. We will also denote by Ψh\Psi_{h} the nearby cycle functor for bounded complexes with constructible cohomology (cf [8] §1).

Let us explain the method we use to compute the formal invariants. We note that if a summand Rα​eαR_{\alpha}e^{\alpha} shows up in the formal decomposition of a ℂ{t}⟨∂t⟩\mathbb{C}\{t\}\langle\partial_{t}\rangle-module 𝒩0\mathcal{N}_{0} after a ramification ρ\rho, then RαR_{\alpha} is the formal regular part of ((ρ∗​𝒩)​e−α)0((\rho^{*}\mathcal{N})e^{-\alpha})_{0}. This formal regular part can be recovered from the specialization of (ρ∗​𝒩)​e−α(\rho^{*}\mathcal{N})e^{-\alpha} at the origin (cf. Example 5.2.1 in [7]). Moreover, as RαR_{\alpha} is localized at the origin, the rank of RαR_{\alpha} and the characteristic polynomial of the monodromy of RαR_{\alpha} can be computed using the nearby cycles module of (ρ∗​𝒩)​e−α(\rho^{*}\mathcal{N})e^{-\alpha} at the origin. One of the main results we use is the commutation of the specialization functor (resp. nearby cycles functor) with proper direct images (cf. Theorem 9.4.19.4.1 in [7] for complexes of 𝒟\mathcal{D}-modules and Theorem 4.8−14.8-1 in [17] for 𝒟\mathcal{D}-modules). This property reduces the proof of Theorem 0.1 to local analytic computations on a suitable blowing-up space of D×ℙ1D\times\mathbb{P}^{1} above (0,∞)(0,\infty). It is also the main argument in the proof of Theorem 0.3.

1. Direct image of holonomic 𝒟\mathcal{D}-module of exponential type: the case of projections

This section is devoted to the proof of Theorems 0.1 and 0.2. We first note that Theorem 0.1 (2)(2) induces the construction of the Newton polygon (Theorem 0.1 (1)(1)).

Let s∈ℕ∗s\in\mathbb{N}^{\ast}.
